title: Map local codes to ICD-10 for the district report
instructions:
## Three facilities, three code lists

Each facility's records system uses its own diagnosis codes. The district report needs ICD-10. A **concept_map** table maps local codes to ICD-10; some local codes are not mapped yet.

Tables: **encounters** (id, facility, local_code, visit_date) and **concept_map** (local_code, icd10, icd_title).

## Do this

Produce the district report: `icd10`, `title`, `encounters` (count), one row per ICD-10 code, with every unmapped encounter gathered into a row whose icd10 is `'UNMAPPED'` and title `'Not mapped'`. Order by encounters descending, then icd10.

A `LEFT JOIN` from encounters to the map keeps the unmapped ones; `COALESCE` supplies the placeholder values. Notice that different local codes can map to the same ICD-10 code and must be counted together.

initialState.sql:
SELECT m.icd10, m.icd_title AS title, COUNT(*) AS encounters
FROM encounters e
JOIN concept_map m ON m.local_code = e.local_code
GROUP BY m.icd10, m.icd_title
ORDER BY encounters DESC, m.icd10;

hints: Change the JOIN to a LEFT JOIN so encounters without a mapping survive.
Group by the COALESCEd expressions (`GROUP BY 1, 2`), not the raw columns.

checks.label: The ICD-10 district report, with unmapped encounters shown
checks.expectedQuery: SELECT COALESCE(m.icd10, 'UNMAPPED') AS icd10, COALESCE(m.icd_title, 'Not mapped') AS title, COUNT(*) AS encounters FROM encounters e LEFT JOIN concept_map m ON m.local_code = e.local_code GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY encounters DESC, icd10

checks.label: It keeps unmapped encounters with a LEFT JOIN
checks.message: An inner join silently drops every encounter whose local code has no mapping, which is the thing the district most needs to see.

realityNote: FHIR ConceptMap resources and terminology servers do this mapping at scale; the unmapped row is what a terminology steward works through each month.
